# Lynn Conway
Lynn Conway (1938–2024) was an influential American computer scientist and electrical engineer known for her pioneering contributions to computer architecture and VLSI (very-large-scale integration) design. She began her career at IBM, where she invented dynamic instruction scheduling for the Advanced Computing Systems (ACS) supercomputer project, leading to the first superscalar processor design. After transitioning and being dismissed by IBM in 1968, Conway restarted her career, eventually joining Xerox PARC, where she led the "LSI Systems" group and co-developed the industry-changing Mead–Conway VLSI chip design methodology. Her work, including the textbook "Introduction to VLSI Systems," fundamentally reshaped chip design, fostered the electronic design automation industry, and led to the MOSIS prototyping service, which democratized access to state-of-the-art chip fabrication.
Conway was a key architect of the DARPA Strategic Computing Initiative and later became a professor at the University of Michigan, specializing in computer engineering and user interface design. She also became a prominent transgender rights activist, widely recognized for sharing her personal journey and advocating for equal opportunities in STEM fields. Conway's legacy includes numerous honors, such as induction into the National Academy of Engineering, Fellow of IEEE, the Computer Pioneer Award, and induction into the National Inventors Hall of Fame in 2023. Her career exemplifies both technical innovation and courage, inspiring inclusivity and diversity in engineering and technology. Conway died on June 9, 2024, at the age of 86.
